name: sendcutsend
description: SendCutSend: laser-cut sheet and plate (router / waterjet for plastics and composites), with bending, tapping, countersinking, PEM hardware, deburring, tumbling, anodizing, powder coating and plating. Every figure carries the page it was read on and the page's own words.
how_read: plain page fetches on 2026-11-15, no account, no upload, no quote. Per-thickness 'View specs' tables on the material pages (minimum hole, minimum bridge, tap hole-to-edge, countersink centre-to-edge, die width) are loaded by script from the ordering application and were NOT read.
sigma_rule: a published +/- tolerance is taken as two standard deviations, the convention of mechloop/tolerance/process.py

notes: Thicker gauges (.190″–.500″) may show light dross that can be removed easily.
Design holes no smaller than material thickness. Keep holes and cutouts 1.5–2× material thickness away from edges to prevent warping or distortion. (best results, not a minimum)
Not in the bending table: SendCutSend does not bend 6061.

steel.grade: A1008 cold rolled up to .135″ (3.43 mm); A36/A1018 HRP&O (hot rolled, pickled and oiled) from .187″ (4.75 mm)
notes: Mild steel is strong and resilient, but it will oxidize (rust) if left unprotected.
Outdoors or humid environments: Requires plating or powder coating to prevent rust.
The deburring table has no .187″ row for mild steel (rows run .135″ then .250″); the plating table starts at .187″, so cold-rolled sheet up to .135″ can be powder coated but not zinc plated here.
Services: deburring, countersinking, tapping only (no anodizing, no powder coat listed).
The page's FAQ gives a minimum cut size of .750″ x 1.00″; its header and the min/max chart give .5″ x 1.00″ / 0.5″ x 0.75″.

properties_published.temperature: will still deform or degrade at prolonged temperatures above ~185–200°F

notes: The material page lists two thicknesses (.125″ laser cut, .270″ CNC routed); the min/max chart also lists .187″ (CNC router); the tapping and countersinking tables list .125″ and .250″.
Services: countersinking and tapping only. No deburring, tumbling or coating.
Routed parts keep fixturing tabs about 0.1875″ wide and a 0.063″ inside corner radius.

hole_min_t_ratio.verbatim: Laser Cutting | At least 50% of material thickness ... Holes smaller than the minimum will distort, char, or fail to cut.
hole_min_t_ratio.note: 'For laser and waterjet, the exact minimum changes with the material and thickness. The current values for every stock we carry live on each material's page.' Those per-thickness values were not readable.

web_min_t_ratio.verbatim: We recommend that hole diameters and bridging widths be no less than 50% of the material thickness. For example, on a 0.125” thick part, this would mean having 0.0625” between all of your cut features, or cut features and the edge of your part.

web_preferred_t_ratio.verbatim: For strength and cut quality reasons, we would prefer that wall thickness or bridging be closer to 1X – 1.5X the material thickness.
web_preferred_t_ratio.checked_by: holes_too_close / hole_too_close_to_edge (general rules, same 1 x thickness)

hole_to_edge_recommended_d_ratio.verbatim: we generally recommend keeping your holes at least 1X their diameter from an edge and slots at least 1.5X their width away from edges or other cut features

cut_tolerance_mm.verbatim: Laser: ±0.005″ on parts under 12″, ±0.010″ on parts over 12″

cut_tolerance_over_12in_mm.verbatim: Laser: ±0.005″ on parts under 12″, ±0.010″ on parts over 12″

cut_tolerance_meaning.verbatim: any given cut feature or perimeter geometry may be +/-.005″, or whatever the cut tolerance for that material and thickness is, in either the X or Y axis

common_line_gap_mm.verbatim: The actual gap between common-nested parts runs 0.006″ to 0.012″ depending on material (kerf)

inside_corner_laser.verbatim: Laser Cutting | Approximately the kerf width (very small)

edge_over_187.verbatim: Materials over .187″ thick will show small striations and an abrasive edge. Add deburring for a cleaner finish.

removed_max_fraction.verbatim: In general, removing around 50% of the material starts to increase the likelihood it will warp.

flatness.verbatim: NOT PUBLISHED: no flatness figure is given for cut parts. 'Sometimes, there's nothing you can do, and warping just happens'; 'often warped parts can't be deburred'.

tap_hole_to_edge.verbatim: Keep the center of any tapped hole at least this distance from other cut features: (tap hole size ÷ 2) + minimum tap hole-to-edge distance for the material. The minimum tap hole-to-edge distance varies by material and thickness. Find it on each material info page.
tap_hole_to_edge.note: per-material value NOT READ (script-loaded). The one worked example published: .063″ (1.6 mm) for .125″ 5052 (how-to-apply-hole-distance-specifications).

tap_direction.verbatim: Tapping direction is perpendicular to the main surface only. All threads are right-hand

tap_powder.verbatim: Tapped holes are not plugged before coating; expect to chase threads after

tap_drill_mm.verbatim: Model your hole at the size listed below for the tap you want. We automatically resize laser cut holes to the correct drill size. M3 x 0.5 | 0.102″ | 2.60 ; M4 x 0.7 | 0.134″ | 3.41 ; M5 x 0.8 | 0.170″ | 4.32

countersink_min_thickness_mm.verbatim: countersink table: no row thinner than .125″ has a size (5052/6061 .040″–.100″: N/A)

countersink_depth_max_t_ratio.verbatim: Max countersink depth | Should not exceed 60% of material thickness

countersink_file.verbatim: Draw only the minor hole in your CAD file. Do not include the major diameter; the countersink is machined to the correct size automatically.

bend_angle_tol_deg.verbatim: Sheet metal bend angle tolerance: Bends up to 24″: +/- 1° ; Bends longer than 24″: +/- 2°
bend_angle_tol_deg.checked_by: bend_tolerance (equals mechloop's class value 0.5 deg one sigma)

bend_position_tol_mm.verbatim: Bend-to-edge tolerance: +/- 0.015″ (each additional bend adds at least 0.015″)
bend_position_tol_mm.checked_by: bend_tolerance (equals mechloop's class value 0.19 mm one sigma)

bend_radius.verbatim: Bend radius and K factor are set per material thickness ... we don't offer custom bend radii.

bend_hole_distance.verbatim: Tapped holes near bends: Place tapped holes at least ½ the full die width away from the bend line. (.125″ 5052: bottom die width 0.630″, so 0.315″)
bend_hole_distance.note: die widths per thickness NOT READ (script-loaded)

bend_u_channel.verbatim: For U-channel and C-channel bends: Sheet metal: base must be at least 2x the flange length (2:1 ratio)

deburr_result.verbatim: Parts are burr-free, smooth, and ready to use, but not perfectly cosmetic. Some edges will be sharp, while others may have slight rounding. Small machining tabs will remain on edges. ... aggressive edge softening must be done after delivery.

deburr_faces_only.verbatim: our deburring process only contacts the top and bottom face of the material, so it will not fully remove edge dross

deburr_steel_rust.verbatim: Deburred Mild Steel is more prone to rusting, and is not recommended for outdoor use unless it's coated.

tumble_part_mm.verbatim: Min part size (flat) | .5″ x 1.5″ ; Max part size (flat) | 4″ x 7″

tumble_result.verbatim: Tumbling is for deburring and edge softening only ... Expect rounded, uniform edges, not a specific radius. Holes and cutouts: Features smaller than 0.5″ won't be fully processed inside. For tumbling plus anodizing, plating, or powder coating, submit a custom quote request.

powder_thickness_mm.verbatim: Coating thickness: Adds .002″–.005″ per side (.004″–.010″ total). Account for this in areas with tight clearances or small holes.

powder_tabs.verbatim: Tabs / micro joints: Not removed prior to coating. Visible through powder coat. Typically .015″–.030″ wide, ~.010″ tall.

anodize_thickness_mm.verbatim: Type II anodizing adds ~0.0002″–0.0009″ per side to part dimensions

anodize_conductivity.verbatim: Anodizing is non-conductive. Scratches will expose raw aluminum beneath

anodize_hanging_hole_mm.verbatim: Required hanging hole | ≥ .063″ (1.60 mm) ; Deburring is preselected on all anodized sheet metal parts.

plating_thickness_mm.verbatim: Zinc plating adds approximately .0003″ per side; nickel adds approximately .0002″ per side

hardware.verbatim: We offer three types of PEM® hardware: nuts, standoffs, and studs. Hardware is installed after anodizing and plating. Hardware is installed before powder coating. Nut, M3 (S-M3-0): hole in sheet .168″, minimum sheet thickness .031″, hole centre to edge .250″, centre to centre .336″.

file_format.verbatim: 2D vector files (preferred for flat cuts): .DXF (preferred), .DWG, .EPS, .AI. Scale 1:1. Inch units are preferred. Mm is fine if you keep it consistent between your file and your quote inputs. We don't support cm or meter units. Your file should contain only your part: strip out dimensions, notes, borders, title blocks. Convert all text to outlines. Closed contours only. No intersecting or shared lines. Single layer for cut paths. Best practice: one part per file.

file_holes_services.verbatim: For hole services (countersinking, dimple forming, hardware, tapping), model simple through-holes and add the service in the app after upload. Model the part at the thickness you'll order.

billet_cnc.verbatim: We offer 6061 T6 Aluminum for CNC machining services. Maximum overall part size: 7” x 7” x 12”. CNC milled parts will have an overall tolerance of +/- .005”. Sharp edges will have a .010” / .254mm edge break. Internal features will have a minimum radius of .0625” (1.587mm).

basis.pos: half of +/-0.127 mm ('Laser: ±0.005″ on parts under 12″')
basis.hole_sd: half of +/-0.127 mm on a cut feature's size
basis.pattern: class value kept: no hole-to-hole figure is published
basis.flat: class value kept: no flatness figure is published

basis.pos: half of +/-0.254 mm ('±0.010″ on parts over 12″')
basis.hole_sd: half of +/-0.127 mm: a hole is a feature under 12 in

bend_tolerance.basis: half of +/-1 deg and +/-0.015 in (0.381 mm), bends up to 24 in

material_rules.text: a cut part's thickness must be one the shop stocks in that material (within 0.05 mm)
the material must be in the shop's cutting chart
6061-T6, cast plate and Delrin are not in the bending table; 5052-H32, mild steel and 304 are
carbon steel needs a declared finish (meta['finish']: 'powder_coat', 'zinc', 'nickel', 'paint', 'oil' or 'bare' with a reason): 'it will oxidize (rust) if left unprotected'
zinc or nickel plating is listed for mild steel from .187 in (4.75 mm) only
anodizing: 5052, 6061, 7075 from .063 in, parts 1 x 3 in to 23 x 23 in

anodizing is non-conductive and powder coat insulates: a protective-earth bond needs a masked or scraped contact, a serrated washer or a dedicated bare stud; powder adds 0.05-0.13 mm per side to every fit
Delrin: 3.18 mm is laser cut at +/-0.23 mm (.009 in); 4.75 and 6.86 mm are routed at +/-0.127 mm with fixturing tabs and 1.6 mm inside corners; no deburring or coating
a flatness-critical plate (print bed, fixture) should be cast tooling plate at a stocked thickness (MIC-6: 6.35, 9.53, 12.7 mm) so its faces stay as supplied

not_published: per-thickness minimum hole, minimum bridge, tap hole-to-edge, countersink centre-to-edge and bending die width: on the material pages behind 'View specs', loaded by script; not read
edge-break radius after deburring or tumbling (explicitly not controlled)
hole-to-hole position tolerance separate from the general cut tolerance
kerf width per material (only the 0.006-0.012 in common-line gap)
